evidence.quote: In our discussions so far, participants have indicated that they thought it would be appropriate to reconsider the language around shortfalls.
And at our meeting last week, we had a similar take on average inflation targeting.
We may be entering a period of more frequent, and potentially more persistent, supply shocks—a difficult challenge for the economy and for central banks.
Anchored expectations are critical to everything we do, and we remain fully committed to the 2 percent target today.
The most recent data suggest that 12-month PCE (personal consumption expenditures) inflation was 2.2 percent in April, far below its 7.2 percent peak in 2022.

parsed.rationale: This framework-review speech offers no near-term policy guidance. It leans modestly hawkish by signaling a move away from shortfalls and average inflation targeting, and by citing higher neutral rates and risks of more frequent supply shocks.
